decision.topic: DB substrate before durable tenancy/outbox/audit evidence
decision.note: The approved option fixes the evidence rule: PR-02 durable isolation, PR-04 outbox and PR-06 audit claims must execute on an explicitly approved early DB substrate rather than on provisional contracts. It builds nothing and it does not create the queue amendment that would schedule the work.

immutableRefs.note: Approval intake, EPOCH-03 chain, registry, gap addendum, the KGA-D06 handoff, the base execution queue and the KGA-D10 record are read by digest only; application state lives in the application-state ledger.

invariants: The approved early-minimal-db option is a governance evidence rule, recorded PLANNING_ONLY, VALID_BLOCKED and gated NO_GO.
Approving a substrate is not building one: no schema is created, no RLS policy is applied, no migration is written or run, and no transaction, outbox or audit implementation exists.
No runtime is started and no code start is permitted; when the substrate is eventually built the executor is human-developer-only.

The queue amendment that would schedule the early substrate after PR-01 is a separate User/Admin decision: queuePatch stays null, no amendment is created and the base queue stays byte-identical with PR-01 as the only next-actionable item.
PR-08 remains the DB substrate owner in the base queue and stays blocked; none of the seven affected items is unblocked, reordered or renumbered here.
The KGA-D06 handoff stays byte-identical read-only evidence with both options still candidate-unselected; this record carries the selection instead of rewriting the handoff.

KGA-D10 evidence is preserved: shared-schema with FORCE RLS deny-by-default stands, mandatory RLS is not weakened, and its deferral to the D06 substrate is not discharged by this planning-only record.
The registry keeps all ten decisions pending and unselected; the closure intake and EPOCH-03 chain are read by digest only.
No planning artifact here is runtime implementation evidence, a code-start permit or a readiness claim.
nonGoals: do not create, generate or apply any database schema, RLS policy, migration, transaction, outbox or audit implementation
do not start a runtime, permit a code start, or claim durable persistence evidence from an approved evidence rule
do not create the queue amendment, patch the base queue, or change any PR identity, order, status or blockedBy field
do not split, renumber or redefine PR-08, and do not unblock any affected item
do not rewrite the KGA-D06 handoff in place or mark either of its options selected
do not discharge the KGA-D10 tenancy enforcement deferral, weaken mandatory RLS, or change the selected physical strategy
do not mutate generated nodes, the registry, the closure intake or the EPOCH-03 chain, and do not write platform or kernel product code

rollback.trigger: any substrate capability flips to implemented, a code start or runtime is permitted, the queue bytes, ordering, next-actionable item or a PR status change, an amendment or queue patch appears, the handoff or KGA-D10 record bytes drift, the tenancy deferral is discharged, or a fail-closed gate flag flips
rollback.action: revert this substrate record, its application-state row, the attestation contract, tests, pack sections and gate wiring as one shard
